parameters.comment:
EV Wallet HK — Shell Recharge (Shell Hong Kong) polling workflow.

Provider: shell
Endpoint: https://api.shell.com.hk/recharge/stations (PLACEHOLDER — replace with the real partnership URL once signed. Until then the call is expected to 4xx and the workflow's StopAndError branch will log + alert via the global error workflow.).

Schedule: every 30 minutes (cron */30 * * * *), 30 minutes offset.

Expected runtime: ~3–10s.

Failure modes:
  Shell API down / 4xx → HTTP Request retries 3× then StopAndError.
  * Paywall / 403 (no key) → StopAndError.
  * FastAPI 5xx → retry then StopAndError.

Idempotency: upsert keyed on (provider_code='shell', external_id). Idempotent on repeat.

QR code format: shell://<POLE_EXTERNAL_ID>-<STATION_EXTERNAL_ID>-<HMAC_SHA256_TRUNC_8>.

Calls our own FastAPI proxy endpoint (Agent A owns). The proxy abstracts the upstream provider URL so this workflow never has to know whether we hit the provider directly or via a paid aggregator. EVW_API_BASE_URL must be configured or n8n throws at node-start.

Run-once-per-item because n8n auto-iterates top-level arrays when the HTTP node returns a JSON array. Each item is one station record from the provider. The code maps the provider's native shape into the canonical ChargingStation + Pole[] + HourlyRate[] shape and signs each pole's QR code with the shared QR_HMAC_SECRET.

Single endpoint that takes (provider_code, external_id, station, poles[], replace_rates) and atomically upserts in one Postgres transaction. FastAPI does the provider-code→id resolution and the unique-key dance so this n8n layer stays simple. See Agent A's /api/v1/internal/stations/upsert endpoint contract.
